evals.prompt: Review the Devices screen in this folder for UI and UX problems. Read DevicesPage.tsx, devices.css and notes.md. For each problem give the element, what is wrong, and the fix. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: A findings list covering the planted violations, with fixes, and no findings against the two components notes.md marks as correct.
expectations: Flags that row actions are hidden until hover (opacity 0) and so are not discoverable on touch or before hover; fix keeps them visible at rest
Flags that the Edit button is omitted for retired rows so the Delete button shifts position between rows; fix keeps a fixed slot (Edit shown disabled with a reason, or a reserved slot)
Flags that the tabs reorder by click count; fix keeps a fixed tab order
Flags the search input that uses a placeholder as its only label; fix adds a visible label
Flags the status shown as a colour-only dot (no text)

Flags the clickable status dot as an unrecognisable, non-keyboard control that retires the device at once; fix is a real menu button (status text plus a chevron or similar hint) listing allowed transitions, with confirmation or undo for retiring
Flags the 'Are you sure?' confirmation on a routine edit; fix removes it or, where a confirmation stays, names the action and object with outcome-named buttons instead of OK/Cancel
Flags that Delete is permanent with neither confirmation nor undo
Flags the 'Error 500' toast as unhelpful; fix states the problem in plain language with the next step, shown persistently or in context
Flags that 'No devices.' shows while data is still loading; fix shows a loading state and a real empty state with a next step
Flags the three stacked banners (including a promo) taking space above the content; fix merges or removes them
Flags two primary buttons in the header; fix keeps one primary action
Flags the sortable Tag header built as a clickable div (not a button, no aria-sort, no visible direction)
Flags window.scrollTo(0, 0) after saving as losing the user's place
Does not report the IconButton tooltips or accessible names, or the pagination, as problems

States each business rule it assumes (for example whether retiring or deleting can be undone, or who may delete) as an assumption, including inside any dialog or message text it proposes, and invents no rule the files do not state

evals.prompt: Our product owner wants four changes to the Devices table: (1) hide row actions that are unavailable for a row, to save space; (2) order the tabs by how often each user clicks them; (3) add an 'Are you sure?' dialog to every Save; (4) make the table denser with 18 px rows and 16 px icon buttons. Give a recommendation for each.
evals.expected_output: One recommendation per request, resolving each against the rules with a concrete alternative.
expectations: (1) Advises against hiding per-row unavailable actions because buttons would shift; recommends keeping the slot with the action disabled and its reason, hiding only actions the role can never use
(2) Advises against usage-ordered tabs because users rely on fixed positions; recommends a fixed order (the most used tab first and selected by default is acceptable)
(3) Advises against a confirmation on every Save; recommends undo for reversible changes and confirmation only for irreversible ones
(4) Accepts denser rows only above the accessibility floor: icon button targets at least 24 by 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8), recovering space by removing chrome first

evals.prompt: Review the contract request wizard and the contract record view in this folder for UI and UX problems. Read ContractRequestPage.tsx, ui.css and notes.md. For each problem give the element, what is wrong, and the fix. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: A findings list covering the planted violations, with fixes, and no findings against the components notes.md marks as reviewed.
expectations: Flags the two-column grid for unrelated form fields; fix is a single column
Flags that optional fields (Notes) are not marked and required fields carry no indication
Flags the Reset form button as a data-loss risk; fix removes it
Flags that Back resets the whole form (setForm(initial)); fix keeps the entered values
Flags that the organization is asked again for billing on step 3; fix prefills or offers the step 1 value
Flags the submit button disabled with no reason; fix explains what is missing (or keeps it enabled and validates)
Flags the submit label 'OK'; fix names the result (for example 'Submit request')
Flags the window.alert('Invalid input') error; fix shows errors next to each field, naming the field and the fix (an error summary is acceptable)
Flags the static 'Loading...' for a quote that takes 15 to 40 seconds; fix shows progress or a time estimate with text, and a way to keep working or cancel
Flags the large red Cancel request button being more prominent than the primary action; fix makes it quieter
Flags the preselected marketing and data-sharing checkbox; fix leaves it unchecked
Flags the 'Offer ends in' countdown that restarts as fake urgency; fix removes it
Flags that edit mode in the record view looks the same as view mode (double-click, no visible cue or way to leave); fix makes the mode visible with save and cancel
Flags that saving is possible only with Ctrl+S; fix adds a visible Save button and keeps the shortcut as an accelerator
Flags the tabs that wrap into two rows and mix in-page tabs with navigation links; fix keeps one row and separates the links
Does not report the DatePicker or the Stepper as problems
